rule: adjusted_score desc, total_score desc; dedupe by arXiv id / URL / id / title

papers.title: AGR: Agentic Generative Retrieval with Tool-Augmented Search
papers.authors: Ming Yang, Yaqi Yin, Zhibo Wang, Xiaoze Jiang, Jingwei Zhuo, Chao Zhang, Quanzhi Zhu, Weiguo Zheng, Liang Zeng, Yunfeng ...
papers.summary: Generative retrieval need not encode every available feature up front. AGR requests intent, location, or behavioral evidence while decoding item identifiers, then resumes generation with a compact observation. A Kuaishou online experiment reports a 0.205% increase in requests with strongly relevant top-four results.
papers.key_insight: Feature value depends on the current identifier prefix. Learning when to request evidence can reduce redundant history encoding, although tool use still costs more than the feature-free baseline.

papers.title: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval
papers.authors: Jinming Nian, Jyun-Yu Jiang, Henry Tsai, Yi Fang, Zhirong Liang
papers.summary: An LLM evolves executable semantic-index programs while a tiny retriever screens them. With the target training recipe fixed, NQ320K Recall@100 rises from 85.82% to 90.57%.
papers.key_insight: Index construction and collision handling are coupled. A cheap proxy can rank index changes well, yet become misleading when the search also changes the generator objective.

papers.title: UniRec: A Unified Expressive-Aligned Generative Recommendation Framework for E-commerce
papers.authors: Ziliang Wang, Gaoyun Lin, Xuesi Wang, Shaoqiang Liang, Yili Huang, Weijie Bian, Li Zhang, Mingchen Cai, Jian Dong, Guanx...
papers.summary: Generative recommendation generates a product's semantic IDs layer by layer, and before the first layer it has seen no product-side information at all; this is its gap with discriminative ranking models. When a discriminative model scores a candidate it sees the product's category, shop and brand directly and crosses them with user features. UniRec has the model first generate the product's category and then generate the semantic IDs conditioned on that category, which puts back into the decoding path the product features a discriminative model can use. Launched online, it raised orders by 4.76% and GMV by 5.60%.

papers.title: OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models
papers.authors: Hao Jiang, Peiru Du, Pengfei Yao, Mengting Li, Siyuan Lou, Kuo Cai, Sheng Yu, Qiang Luo, Jian Liang, Ruiming Tang, Fei P...
papers.summary: When a large language model serves as a recommendation foundation model and first writes a natural-language reasoning trace before outputting the next item's semantic ID, the reasoning text is far longer than the semantic ID and holds back both decoding time and throughput. OneLatent appends 3 fixed special tokens after the user context and trains in several steps. First the model learns to reproduce a teacher LLM's reasoning text after these tokens, then it is switched to outputting the target semantic ID directly after them. At serving time only these tokens are appended and no reasoning text is generated. On industrial data its semantic-ID hit rate within the top 64 candidates is 17.44% higher than reason-then-answer, and its inference throughput is 17.49 times that of explicit reasoning.

papers.title: Controllable Generative Recommendation via Guided Token Refinement
papers.authors: Haichao Zhang, Zhixuan Liang, Chong Zhang, Zixi Chen, Wen Wang, Jia Wang
papers.summary: Generative recommenders emit item-ID tokens left to right, so temporary diversity at inference ==can only rewrite one position mid-decode and often produces IDs that do not exist in the catalog==. ReGen uses a bidirectional Transformer to predict all 4 ID tokens at once, subtracts a score only on the coarsest positions for token values common in the user history, remasks low-confidence positions and repredicts, and uses a prefix tree of all legal IDs to drop token values that cannot complete a real item—without changing model parameters. On Amazon Instruments, top-10 category coverage rises from 0.41 to 0.59 while Recall@10 falls only from 0.0427 to 0.0394 (TIGER-MMR falls from 0.0433 to 0.0319 in the same range); without the prefix tree only 27.63% of IDs map to real items.

papers.title: GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix
papers.authors: Lequn Wang, Jiangwei Pan, Linas Baltrunas
papers.summary: The Netflix homepage used to be assembled by a multi-stage recommender that retrieved candidate rows and titles, ranked them separately and then built the page; GenPage instead generates the whole page with one decoder-only Transformer. The homepage is made of rows, each row a theme. User history, account attributes and request information are encoded as a prompt, and the model generates row tokens and title tokens one by one, left to right and top to bottom. Training copies the large-language-model recipe: first pretrain with next-token prediction on homepages that received positive feedback online, then post-train with weighted binary classification or reinforcement learning. The former labels each shown row or title by whether user feedback was positive and weights it by the reward size; the latter optimizes the sum of rewards of all titles shown on the page. In a 14-day A/B test it raised the core user engagement metric Netflix uses for launch decisions by 0.24% and cut end-to-end latency by 20%.

papers.title: Gryphon-v2: One Model in Place of a Cascade - Generate-and-Rank Recommender with Rollout Distillation
papers.authors: Anna Lipkina, Daria Tikhonovich, Viktor Yanush, Mariia Ulianova, Oleg Sorokin, Vladislav Dodonov, Ilya Murzin, Denis Bur...
papers.summary: Gryphon-v2 encodes user history once, generates semantic item IDs, and ranks the resolved items with a small shared-state head. A larger teacher supplies training targets but stays out of serving. Replacing the Yandex Music cascade increased active users by 1.41% in an online experiment.
papers.key_insight: Distill on candidates the generator actually produces as well as logged impressions. This teaches the ranking head its serving distribution while retaining exposure-based supervision; sharing the history encoder then removes redundant online work.

papers.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
papers.authors: He Ma, Lan You, Qiyang Wu, Chen Liu
papers.summary: LightCRS caches frozen multimodal product representations offline and uses a shared query-conditioned module to compare candidates online. HR@1 improves by 35.4% over the strongest baseline.
papers.key_insight: Separate reusable product evidence from dialogue-dependent matching. Query-conditioned fusion enables a compact shared model to serve multiple domains.

papers.title: From Habits to Discovery: Deploying LLMs for Personalized Generative Recommendations at Spotify
papers.summary: Spotify wants the home feed to surface podcasts the user has not yet formed a habit around (under 10 minutes on a show in the past 28 days). GLIDE, based on Llama 3.2 1B, first learns to translate between episode semantic IDs and text, then reads recent episode semantic IDs, region and other text fields, ==a soft-prompt token projected from a collaborative-filtering user vector==, and an instruction to push familiar versus unseen content, and directly generates 30 episode candidates. Offline Recall@30 is 29.9% above a semantic-ID-only variant; online A/B tests show up to +5.4% non-habitual listening and +14.3% new-show discovery while meeting latency SLOs.

papers.title: Coarse-to-Fine Long-term Interest Modeling for Generative Recommendation
papers.authors: Shiteng Cao, Junda She, Ji Liu, Bin Zeng, Chengcheng Guo, Kuo Cai, Qiang Luo, Ruiming Tang, Han Li, Kun Gai, Zhiheng Li,...
papers.summary: Generative recommendation generates the next item's semantic IDs one code at a time, and attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length, so these models usually take only the most recent few dozen behaviors and leave the long-term history unused. GLASS uses the long-term history differently for each semantic ID level. Before generating the first-level code, it averages the item vectors of each first-level code into a prototype. It then splits the cosine-similarity range into equal bins, counts how many long-term history items fall into each bin for each prototype, and passes the concatenated counts of all first-level codes through a small network to get one interest token fed to the encoder. After the first-level code is generated, it uses that code as a retrieval key to pull items of the same broad category from the long-term history, which help generate the last two codes. On TAOBAO-MM, R@1 is 21.57% higher than the strongest baseline; in a two-week A/B test on a short-video platform, recall rose 3 percentage points in absolute terms.

papers.title: Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction
papers.authors: Zhiguang Yang, Yulin Yang, Fuyu Lv, Dan Ou
papers.summary: Taobao search CTR models mainly remember historical clicks through item IDs, so ==the same item with a different main image is almost indistinguishable to the model==. FineSID turns each item image into 30 discrete codes across four VAR tokenizer scales from 1×1 to 4×4, tokenizes titles and OCR text by field, and looks them all up like ordinary ID features; the shared network is first trained on query–item relevance labels from a Qwen3.5 teacher, then fine-tuned with a click head on click logs. Offline AUC is 0.25 points above the HiFormer baseline and 0.38 points higher on cold items; a seven-day Taobao main-search A/B test raised GMV by 0.85%.

papers.title: ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling
papers.authors: Wenhao Li, Qinglin Jia, Chenghou Jin, Zihong Xian, Jiezhou Ji, Yanzhi Liu, Zezheng Wang, Bo Chen, Ruiming Tang, Chaoyi M...
papers.summary: ECHO makes 100K-event histories affordable by retaining reusable original records before candidate-aware retrieval. A full-history teacher supervises selection, while retrieval and aggregation share relevance parameters. Kuaishou reports a 0.613% increase in app usage time in an online test.
papers.key_insight: Compression can preserve individually addressable events rather than only latent interest vectors. Reusable user-level selection moves work out of the request path and leaves candidate-specific matching to a smaller evidence set.

papers.title: A Framework for Value-Aligned Modeling and Robust Experimentation
papers.authors: Krishna Harsha Reddy Kothapalli, Angela Liu, Kamal Nayan Reddy Challa, Pavithra Seshadrivijayakrishnan, Yongpeng Yang, M...
papers.summary: In the Google Discover ads team's model iteration, offline and online results did not line up. The correlation between the change in the conversion model's offline loss and online advertiser value was only 0.1, and many changes that looked better offline failed in the small-traffic A/B stage. This paper weights the offline loss by how much each click is worth to the advertiser, so that a loss decrease corresponds to a value increase. After the changes, the offline-to-online correlation rose to 0.65, and switching two models to the new objective raised online value by 4.7% in total.

papers.title: KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale
papers.authors: Jiahao Hui, Lin Zhu, Ben Tan, Yishen Hu, Jingdong Shu, Zetai Jiang, Xining Ran, Yeshou Cai, Gong Chen, Haijie Gu
papers.summary: KuaFu avoids repeatedly encoding the same content across users and profiling tasks. It caches compact item representations, assembles them chronologically and uses staged training to preserve evidence. Tencent reports a 1.37% overall GMV increase against a long-term holdout.
papers.key_insight: Make items the unit of reuse. Encode shared content once, while preserving actions and sequence order on the user side. The cache then scales with item inventory, supporting more frequent multi-task profile refreshes.

papers.title: FLMNet: Self-Ensemble Distillation from Masks to Seeds for Single-Tower CTR Prediction
papers.authors: Yifan Wang, Yifei Du
papers.summary: CTR self-distillation can be replaced with a computable disagreement penalty. FLMNet keeps gates on clean inputs and distills independently trained towers into one serving model. The distilled model reaches 0.8169 AUC on Criteo.
papers.key_insight: Separate mask disagreement from seed disagreement: regularize the former within a run and distill the latter across runs. The moment formulas require gates that do not read masked intermediate activations.

papers.title: LSNR: Learned Sparse News Recommendations with Attentive User Modeling
papers.authors: David Vos, Andrew Yates, Maarten de Rijke
papers.summary: Encode articles separately, then learn which ones matter. LSNR combines weighted sparse article vectors with a user-level semantic expansion, improving MIND NDCG@10 by about 11% over STAR.
papers.key_insight: Article boundaries matter beyond context length. A lexical path preserves evidence from individual clicks, while a semantic path adds aggregate interests. Gains with a single history article show that truncation is only part of the problem.

papers.title: Predictable Scaling: Efficient Model Exploration via Scaling-Law Prediction
papers.authors: Aishwarya Wesanekar, Sheng-Tao Yang, Jiawei Zang, Flavio Sales Truzzi, Chen Chen, Nader Beigiparast, Shengyuan Huang, Ro...
papers.summary: Predictable Scaling evaluates ranking-model changes with reduced-scale proxies and estimates their full-scale effects using historical learning curves. Training compute falls by 88% and 79% on two industrial ranking models.
papers.key_insight: A useful proxy preserves which changes are better, not merely a small average prediction error. Scaling must be chosen for each architecture: reducing embedding width alone can scramble the ordering of candidate changes.

papers.title: DuoLM: Fast and Effective Personalized Recommendation with Language Models
papers.authors: Jiang Wu, Yutong Song, Hongbo Wang, Guanghe Cao, Jeff Lei Liang
papers.summary: DuoLM precomputes one vector per item and uses a personalized ranker with user history and feedback. Shared history computation and a specialized runtime reduce online work. Throughput reaches about 26,400 candidate scores per second on one H100.
papers.key_insight: Train reusable content representations and personalized judgments jointly. Compression pays off in end-to-end serving only when repeated history prefill, input transmission, and scheduling are reduced too.

papers.title: EASformer: Environment-Action-State Alignment for Industrial Generative Ranking
papers.authors: Bohao Li, Dinglun Cao, Pengcheng Huang, Yingda Tang, Zhiting Zhao, Yi Cao, Jilei Fu, Miao Yan, Tianying Liu, Heng Chang,...
papers.summary: EASformer addresses a mismatch between historical tokens containing observed actions and candidates with no observed action. It separates environment, action and state before matching them. The larger of two reported online eCPM lifts is 3.94%.
papers.key_insight: Attention should compare semantically aligned representations. Separating environmental matching from action prediction also lets masked historical actions reuse the candidate-prediction pathway for self-supervision.

papers.title: SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs
papers.authors: Chunrui Zhang, Gaoyun Lin, Chang Zhou, Zheng Hu, Qiran Song, Shimin Cai, Tao Zhou
papers.summary: SPAR reduces early branch errors in semantic-ID recommendation by retrieving user evidence at every decoding step and balancing traffic across sibling branches. A Youku online experiment reports a 3.95% increase in average watch time per user.
papers.key_insight: Personalization should change with the generated prefix. Inspect user-evidence retrieval and branch-load imbalance together to diagnose early decoding errors that prevent the right item from remaining reachable.

papers.title: The Fusion Tax: A Diagnostic Analysis of When Hybrid Retrieval Hurts
papers.authors: Aaditya Chauhan, Arun Agarwal
papers.summary: Hybrid retrieval fuses the results of term-matching sparse retrieval such as BM25 with those of dense vector retrieval into a single ranking, and it always wins on average. Yet query by query, 13–48% of queries rank worse than the better of the two retrievers on that query. This paper keeps the books differently: it compares nDCG@10 before and after fusion query by query, and treats no fusion as a legitimate option. The authors call this per-query loss the fusion tax. The losses concentrate on queries where only one retriever finds a relevant document, and the other retriever then contributes only noise. Switching to a larger dense encoder or adding a cross-encoder reranker after fusion does not make this tax disappear.

papers.title: pplx-embed-v2-late Technical Report
papers.authors: Markus Krimmel, Louis Milliken, Ekaterina Glazkova, Maximilian Schall, Antoine Chaffin, Sedigheh Eslami, Jonas Golde, De...
papers.summary: Perplexity releases 0.6B and 9B multi-vector retrievers that encode text, images, and document screenshots: each document token stores a 128-d vector, and scoring sums MaxSim of each query vector against document vectors. Both models distill token-by-token from the same 18B teacher, ==so they share one vector space== and a 9B offline document index can be queried by a 0.6B online encoder. On 72 domain retrieval tasks the 9B model averages nDCG@10 81.3%, 1.6 points above nemotron-3-embed-8b; a 0.6B query with a 9B index scores 79.6%, above 78.0% when both ends use 0.6B. On BrowseComp+ the 9B model lets an agent answer 64.0% correctly with the fewest searches.

papers.title: OpenSaC: A Python Library for Search as Code in Deep Research Agents
papers.authors: Qi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua, Ji-Rong Wen
papers.summary: OpenSaC lets research agents write programs that combine search, reading, reranking, and local processing, returning selected evidence to the model. On BrowseComp, it cuts model-token use by 37.8%.
papers.key_insight: Process intermediate evidence in code and preserve source links for reuse. The library reduces repeated model reading, but requires an execution environment. WideSearch row F1 falls slightly, so efficiency gains do not guarantee better answers.

papers.title: FALCA: Falsification-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Deep Search Agents
papers.authors: Zijun Dou, Kun Luo, Chaofan Li, Shuqi Lu, Zheng Liu
papers.summary: Deep search can reinforce an early mistaken hypothesis. FALCA separates answer proposals from independent counterevidence searches and trains research-state revision with hierarchical credit. Its 4B model reaches 56.0% accuracy on BrowseComp.
papers.key_insight: Give counterevidence checking its own context. A useful falsification report names conflicting evidence and unmet constraints, giving the next search a specific gap to resolve.

papers.title: When Agentic Retrieval Fails Silently: Framework and Production Evidence from a Creative AI Assistant
papers.authors: Yan, Liang, Anuj Agarwal, Aditya Reddy Cheruku
papers.summary: In Adobe Express's AI assistant, retrieval metrics that assume the user saw a ranked list and acted on it stop working. The chat entry point has a reformulation rate of 44.4%, higher than the template gallery search served by the same retrieval system, at 33.1%. The reason is that reformulation means different things on the two sides. In the gallery, a user reformulates because the results were irrelevant and they try other words. In chat, most reformulations come after the user sees a generated result and wants to tweak it. More surprising still, the assistant actually called retrieval on only 0.31% of prompts. The paper's evaluation framework measures in three layers: it scores the returned results against relevance labels when retrieval fires, then checks whether the returned assets were used, and finally whether the user exported. Four log fields record the retrieval ID, the full returned list, which asset each action used, and which retrieval that asset came from, linking every use and export back to that retrieval.

papers.title: Chunk Recomputation under Real Document Revisions: Measuring Update Cost and Retrieval Quality of Fixed, Recursive, and Content-Defined Chunking
papers.authors: Yuning Bian, Lele Xu, Yifan Yuan, Xinyu Yin, Chengyan Zhan
papers.summary: Chunking schemes for RAG are almost always compared on one static corpus, yet the documents in a knowledge base keep changing. Each chunk is embedded on its own, so if an edit moves a chunk boundary, the chunks on either side become new embedding inputs even when not a single word in them changed. The authors take adjacent revisions of Chinese and English Wikipedia articles and allow an old vector to be reused only when a chunk's complete embedding input is byte-identical to one in the old version. They compare three chunking methods: non-overlapping fixed-size chunking, paragraph-first recursive chunking and content-defined chunking, which hashes a sliding window of a few words and cuts wherever the hash meets a preset condition. Fixed-size chunking recomputes 57–68% of the new version's embedding input, yet the three methods differ in evidence recall by less than 2 percentage points within each language. Fixed-size chunking shifts everything after the insertion point, so none of the downstream windows can match the old version, which is why it recomputes the most.

papers.title: EG-GRPO: Evidence-Guided Step-level Credit Assignment for Deep Search Agents
papers.authors: Sijia Luo, Mengjie Gao, Yuxiao He, Mengshu Sun, Cuiping Li, Hong Chen, Jing Zhang
papers.summary: EG-GRPO rewards the first search step that finds support for a required claim, then compares actions from similar evidence states. The 4B agent reaches 45.9% accuracy on GAIA.
papers.key_insight: Reward newly acquired evidence rather than repeated citations. Conditioning comparisons on what an agent already knows reduces unfair comparisons between early and nearly finished trajectories; fallback grouping handles sparse state matches.

papers.title: Grounded Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Search Agents
papers.authors: Qirui Liu, Hao Chen, Yi Wen, Weijie Shi, Yao Zhao, Xianhe Chen, Hao Zhao, Xing Tang, Weihong Luo, Yuyu Luo
papers.summary: A search agent can answer correctly without using retrieved evidence. Grounded Credit Assignment separates credit for finding evidence from credit for answering. On the larger evaluated model, it improves average exact match over Search-R1 by 6.3 percentage points.
papers.key_insight: Reward evidence acquisition separately from answer correctness. Otherwise, a lucky answer from memory credits the entire retrieval trace and can improve accuracy while weakening grounding. The proposed correction uses verifiable sub-outcomes without an extra reward model.

papers.title: Directional Posterior Feedback Fusion for Query Reformulation in Dense Retrieval
papers.authors: Yiteng Tu, Qingyi Pan, Weihang Su, Jiaxin Mao, Yiqun Liu, Qingyao Ai
papers.summary: When rewriting a query vector with first-round retrieved documents or an LLM-written hypothetical answer (HyDE), the usual approach averages feedback vectors and interpolates with the original query. DIFF argues that ==each piece of feedback only supports correcting the query along one direction, so other directions should not be pulled back by it==: it subtracts the component parallel to the original query to get each feedback's rotation direction and magnitude, constrains only the projection of the correction onto that direction, weights by query–feedback similarity and group agreement, and solves a K×K linear system—without training any model. On 14 BEIR subsets, bge-base with HyDE rises from 0.5492 to 0.5717 mean NDCG@10; with retrieved-document feedback, vector averaging falls to 0.5045 while DIFF scores 0.5522.

papers.title: Let Agents Design How They Search: Automatic Interface Optimization for Agentic Search
papers.authors: Sangjune An, Jaeyoon Jung, Yumin Choi, Jinheon Baek, Junmo Cho, Sung Ju Hwang, Hae Beom Lee
papers.summary: Korea University and KAIST have Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) design retrieval tools for a search agent: it reads each question's execution log and score, jointly edits pre-generated index files, executable search scripts, and usage instructions, and after 10 rounds keeps the best version on the optimization set. With GPT-5.4-nano as the search agent, BrowseComp-Plus accuracy rises from DCI's 71.6% to 78.4%, and mean nDCG@10 on four BRIGHT subsets from 45.7 to 55.0. Prompt-only optimization reaches 75.6% and 52.0, ==so the rest of the gain comes from the generated index files and search scripts==; handing the interface unchanged to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite still beats DCI (73.9% vs 60.9%).

papers.title: ATTUNE: Agentic Throughput Tuning for LLM Training
papers.authors: Leo Fan, Hongyang Wang, Wenbo Chen, Jingguo Liu, Xian Li, Xuan Wang, Ruochen Wen, Yiming Yan, Hao Wu, Yichuan Li, Qian Q...
papers.summary: Move a large model to a different GPU or framework version, and the training recipe that used to be fastest often no longer is. The recipe settles how the model is split across GPUs, which low-level routines to use, and how GPU data transfers overlap with computation. ATTUNE lets an AI agent able to write code and run commands tune recipes, given a recipe that runs and a budget of GPU-hours; it tries things and analyses bottlenecks on its own. But the real point of the paper lies outside the agent, in a correctness gate run by fixed code the agent cannot change. The model, data, batch size and numeric precision are locked, and any change that would quietly alter what is being trained, such as dropping overflow tokens, is rejected before launch. After fine-tuning jobs for three models switched to the tuned recipes, training ran on average 1.7 times as fast as before, and up to 3.9 times.

papers.title: RemoteANN: A Native Vector Search Engine for Cloud Object Storage
papers.authors: Yutong Gou, Silu Huang, Yue Wang, Jianjun Chen, Cheng Long
papers.summary: RemoteANN co-designs vector indexing and query execution for cloud object storage. Quantized inverted lists, reordered data, merged range reads and local SSD caching reduce remote I/O. At matched target recall, the authors report up to 5.9× higher throughput than representative baselines.
papers.key_insight: The useful optimization target is remote requests per query. Data locality makes request merging and caching effective; faster distance computation alone cannot remove object-store latency.

papers.title: uGDS: A User-Space Development Kit for High-Performance GPU Direct Storage
papers.authors: Jing Wei, Guanyi Chen, Qi Chen, Chuyu Zhang, Zheng Zhou, Chutian Wang, Jian Zhang
papers.summary: When NVIDIA's GDS reads data from SSD straight into GPU memory, the authors measured that 99.6% of the time for asynchronous reads was stuck at the step of submitting requests. Large-model inference services store the KV cache they have already computed on SSDs, so that the next request with the same opening can read it back instead of recomputing, and the speed of this read feeds directly into time-to-first-token. uGDS moves the job of telling the SSD what to do out of the operating-system kernel and into an ordinary program. Data still goes straight from SSD to GPU; what changes is who gives the orders. uGDS's batched reads are up to 12 times as fast as GDS, and plugged into an open-source cache system, the median time-to-first-token for long prompts fell from 1.9 seconds to 0.7 seconds.

papers.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
papers.authors: Liana Patel, Rishabh Ranjan, Ion Stoica, Matei Zaharia, Carlos Guestrin
papers.summary: TokenGate trains an existing model to skip less useful tokens in later layers. Token-gated attention supplies a learning signal for token selection. Across the tested tasks, the authors report up to 11.3× faster time to first token without measured accuracy loss.
papers.key_insight: Token selection can be learned during lightweight adaptation instead of imposed as a fixed heuristic. This targets prefill latency and memory, with an adaptation step required before deployment.

papers.title: E8-QAT: Efficient 2-Bit Quantization-Aware Training with Implicit Lattice Codebooks
papers.authors: Xinyu Lei, Hong Huang, Jiebin Zhang, Hongyu Li, Jinlong Song, Decheng Wu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Sujian Li
papers.summary: Grouped weight quantization avoids an explicit codebook search by projecting onto a structured lattice. At each format’s largest feasible batch, decoding reaches 1.97 times BF16 throughput. This comparison includes the batch-size benefit of lower memory use.
papers.key_insight: Treat storage format and feasible batch size as coupled decisions. Arithmetic lattice projection reduces codebook search overhead, while memory savings create additional serving capacity.

papers.title: Large Flow Language Models
papers.authors: Arnav Chavan, Chanhyuk Lee, Udbhav Bamba, Jaehoon Yoo, Seunghoon Hong
papers.summary: Lafa adapts pretrained autoregressive models into blockwise continuous-flow language models. A single model proposes flow-based drafts and verifies them autoregressively, reaching 2.54 times autoregressive throughput at comparable quality.
papers.key_insight: Drafting and verification can share a model. Retaining autoregressive capability creates a verification path for parallel flow proposals without a separately maintained drafter.

papers.title: Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference
papers.authors: Xiuyi Qin
papers.summary: An independent researcher compares "add 2:4 sparsity" versus "drop one precision tier" on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B under matched storage bits (including sparse indices) and matched nominal compute tiers, with measurements on L40S, H100, and RTX PRO 6000. ==As long as a lower precision is still available, adding 2:4 is both less accurate and slower==: 2:4 + INT8 costs the same storage as INT5. At the FP8 floor, a retrained 2:4 model served by vLLM on H100 raises prefill throughput 27% over dense FP8 with matched GSM8K; but ==during retraining perplexity recovers first while reasoning accuracy recovers much more slowly==.

papers.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
papers.authors: Tianyu Fu, Ruoxi Wang, Zihan Min, Zhongqi Ren, Zhihao Li, Tengxuan Liu, Shengxu Mu, Hanling Zhang, Yu Wang
papers.summary: When an agent goes back and forth with tools such as search, web pages and code execution for hundreds of turns, it pays a recurring cost. On every turn the model re-reads the KV cache of everything that came before, and reading this old cache accounts for 82.4% of total inference cost. The usual way to save money is to delete or summarize old messages, but any edit to earlier text invalidates all the cache after it, so everything from the edit point onward has to be recomputed. The authors work at a different layer: leave the text history untouched and drop only selected entries from the cache, while the remaining entries are reused as they are. A simple policy of keeping the cache of only the 12 most recent tool outputs beats the common approach of summarizing at the length limit, with a pass rate 1.7 percentage points higher on average across four agent benchmarks and 27.7% lower average cost.

papers.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
papers.authors: Irene Tenison, Abdulrahman Alabdulkareem, Daniel Karl I. Weidele, Nima Dehmamy, Dan Gutfreund
papers.summary: The KV cache a large model keeps in GPU memory grows with the text, and one way to compress it is to make the vector stored for each word shorter, but most existing methods only save storage. They store short vectors, yet at compute time must first restore them to full length, so computation balloons. RACE finds a way to shorten vectors without restoring them. Position encoding rotates each pair of adjacent numbers in a vector together, so as long as whole pairs are kept, the short vector can still be rotated directly. The pairs kept are those where queries and keys have the largest sum of squares on a small batch of text, and that choice is written directly into the model weights. On Llama-3.2-3B, with vectors halved and an input of 256,000 tokens, overall throughput rises to 1.79 times and time-to-first-token falls 43.2%.

papers.title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity
papers.authors: Sahil Joshi, Prithvi Dixit, Aryan Katiyar, Agniva Chowdhury, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Anshumali Shrivastava, Aditya Desai, Ku...
papers.summary: In long-context decoding, every generated token reads the whole KV cache from HBM, so the longer the context, the slower attention gets. Sparse attention reads only a small subset of tokens, but at 50× sparsity existing methods fall far short of dense attention. The idea of SSA is that high-scoring tokens are always kept, the remaining long tail is sampled by proxy score, and each sampled token is up-weighted by its probability of being sampled. The proxy score is a quick attention estimate from compressed keys. After softmax, all probabilities are multiplied by one common factor, and tokens that reach one are kept outright. The factor is chosen so that the number kept plus the scaled probabilities of the other tokens equals the budget exactly. The rest of the budget is sampled with replacement by that probability, a token drawn more than once counts once, and its weight is divided by its chance of being drawn at least once. At the same sparsity, on AIME 2025 with Qwen3.5-9B, SSA scores 59.8 versus 36.7 for PQCache.
